label: UniFi Switch Flex 2.5G
description: Ubiquiti USW-Flex-2.5G-8 - 8x 2.5GbE RJ45, 1x 10GbE RJ45 (the PoE+ power inlet), 1x 10G SFP+; powered by PoE+ on the 10G RJ45 or by a USB-C adapter, no PoE output.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/usw-flex-2-5g-8 (server-rendered table): **Port Layout 2.5 GbE RJ45 8 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M) / 10 GbE RJ45 1 (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M) / 10G SFP+ 1 (10G/1G)**; **Max. Power Consumption 14W with PoE input, 14W with AC adapter input**; **Power Method (1) USB Type-C, 5V DC, 3A (1) PoE+**; **Power Input Method USB Input / PoE**; **Supported Voltage Range 4.8-5.2V DC/USB, 44V-57V PoE**. The sheet carries no PoE Ports, Max PoE Output or Total PoE Availability row at all - unlike its PoE sibling (devices/ubiquiti/usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe.json, which prints "PoE Ports PoE++ 8" and 196 W of availability). This model sources no power, so all eight 2.5G sockets are declared poeIn: false rather than inheriting the engine guess. Which socket is the inlet: https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/usw-flex-2-5g-8 (read 2026-11-28) - "Flexible, 8-port 2.5 GbE switch with a 10 GbE RJ45/SFP+ combination uplink port that can be powered with a USB-C or PoE+ adapter." The PoE+ inlet is therefore the 10G RJ45 (Port 9 in this sheet), and it draws the vendor's 14 W ceiling; the 2.5G bank and the SFP+ cage carry no power either way.
